newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland may call off Ruch sale talks -Kaczmarek.
newsitem.headline: Poland may call off Ruch sale talks -Kaczmarek.

text.p: Poland may call off talks on the sale of news-stand chain Ruch SA with France's Hachette Distribution Services if it fails to make a firm financial offer by the end of November, a deputy treasury minister said.
"I am awaiting from the investor a clear statement on whether he is going to negotiate the financial conditions of the deal or not," Wieslaw Kaczmarek told a news briefing.
He said that if talks with Hachette failed, the ministry, which had picked Hachette for exclusive negotiations, might renew talks with other bidders or announce a new tender.

Kaczmarek said another privatisation project which had hit rough waters -- and would not meet this year's deadline -- was the planned sell-off of the wholesale and retail foodstuffs chain Polski Hurt Spozywczy (PHS).
"Efforts to privatise this company failed and now in order to keep it alive it needs to be subjected to radical restructuring," he said.

He also called on the transport ministry to support the tentative agreement with Adtranz, which agreed to pay $3.7 million for the troubled Pafawag SA rolling-stock maker and invest in the company's development.

Kaczmarek said that for the deal to be finalised the Polish State Railways (PKP) would have to confirm by the end of this month their plans to place orders with Pafawag, which so far the transport ministry, which oversees PKP, has failed to do.
"The agreement is in force until the end of November and by then Pafawag, PKP and the investor should reach an agreement. If they fail to do so the deal will not be concluded," he said.
"The transport ministry has so far failed to make its position clear," he added.
But Kaczmarek said the ministry would make progress with several other privatisation schemes, paving the way for their sell-off early next year.
"We expect to submit issue prospectuses of the Hutment (non ferrous metals firm), Swiece (paper maker) and Impexmetal (metals trader) before the end of the year," Kaczmarek said.
